chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad who said:
A man wanted to marry off his slave girl to a free man and stipulated that whenever he wished, he could separate them. Is that permissible for him? I was made your ransom, or not? So he wrote: Yes.

key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: I was made your ransom (polite address)

ai.seo_question: Can a master stipulate the right to divorce his slave girl and her free husband?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Al-Rayan ibn Shabib conveys the Imam’s ruling on a specific marital stipulation where a master maroffs his slave woman to a free man with the retained right to dissolve the union at will. This highlights the flexibility of *khitab* (conditions) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating that the master’s ownership rights can extend to the marital bond under agreed terms. The ruling underscores the practical application of contractual freedom within the framework of slavery, a key topic in classical fiqh.
